turns.prompt_text: I got a question, I use google to store most of my passwords, however I do not know the google password itself
turns.response_html:
That is a bit of a "key locked in the car" situation, isn't it? It's surprisingly common since we all rely so heavily on autofill these days.

Since you are likely already signed into your Google account on your primary devices (like your Mac Mini or MacBook Air), you have a few ways to tackle this without needing the password immediately.

1. Check Your Saved Passwords (The "Backdoor")

If you are currently signed into Google Chrome on your computer, you might actually have the Google password saved inside the manager itself, or you can use your computer's local credentials to see it.

  • On Mac: Open Chrome, go to Settings > Autofill and Passwords > Google Password Manager.
  • Search for "https://www.google.com/search?q=google.com" or "accounts.https://www.google.com/search?q=google.com".
  • When you click the "eye" icon to reveal the password, it will usually ask for your Mac's login password or Touch ID, not your Google password.

2. Account Recovery (The Official Way)

If it’s not saved there, you’ll need to go through the recovery process. Since you have your phone and active email access, this should be straightforward:

  1. Go to the Google Account Recovery page.
  2. Enter your email address.
  3. When it asks for a password, click "Try another way."
  4. Google will likely send a prompt to your phone or a verification code to your recovery email/SMS.

3. Pro-Tips for Success

To make the recovery process smoother, Google’s automated systems look for familiarity:

  • Use your usual device: Try the recovery from your Mac Mini or MacBook rather than a new device.
  • Stay on your home Wi-Fi: Being in a familiar location (like your place in Ankeny or Ames) helps verify it's actually you.

A quick heads-up: Once you do get back in or reset it, I’d recommend grabbing those Backup Codes from your Security settings. They are a lifesaver for situations just like this!

Do you have a recovery phone number or a secondary email linked to the account that you can still access?

That’s great news—having that access makes this much easier. Since you have your recovery methods ready, here is the most direct way to get this sorted:

The Reset Process

  1. Go to the Google Account Recovery page.
  2. Enter your email and click Next.
  3. When it asks for your password, select "Try another way" at the bottom.
  4. Google will offer to send a verification code to your recovery phone number or email.
  5. Once you enter that code, you'll be prompted to create a new password.

A Quick Suggestion for Later

Since you're a fan of productivity tools like Obsidian or Notion, once you’ve reset your password, you might want to create a "Digital Emergency Kit" note. Don't store the password itself there, but you can keep those Google Backup Codes (one-time use codes you can print out) in a secure spot.

It’s also worth checking if your iPhone or Mac has the password stored in Keychain—sometimes it saves a copy there even if it's not showing up in Chrome.

Were you able to get the verification code sent to your device?
